name: Bank of Baroda
business_summary: Bank of Baroda is India's second-largest public-sector bank by business (government holds ~64%), with retail, MSME, agri, corporate and treasury segments and a large international franchise (UAE, UK, Africa, Asia; ~15% of advances, model estimate). Q2 FY27 net profit Rs6,532cr (+35.8% y/y, record; aided by lower provisions and one-offs incl. NSE stake sale gains), NII Rs13,026cr (+9%), global NIM 2.74% (2.96% a year ago), GNPA 1.78%, NNPA 0.37%. FY27 guidance raised to 13-15% credit growth and 11-13% deposit growth. Trades at 0.74x book, P/E 5.4, dividend yield ~3.4%. Overhangs: ECL transition, NMC/BR Shetty $15bn suit, margin compression, and a rising-rate cycle.

revenue_mix.geography: India ~80% / international ~20% of advances (approx., model estimate)

revenue_mix.segment: Fee, forex and other non-interest income

exposures.mechanism: Two channels. (1) Treasury MTM: investment book ~Rs5 lakh cr (model estimate), AFS/FVTPL ~Rs1.3 lakh cr x modified duration ~3 x 0.25% = ~Rs1,000cr pre-tax = ~Rs730cr post-tax = ~0.6% of Rs1.29 lakh cr mcap (one-off, partly reverses). (2) Cost of equity: P/B 0.74 on ROE 12.7%; +25bp G-sec passes ~50% to CoE => P/B ~-2.5%. Sum ~-3, shrunk to -1.4 for persistence/offset from higher asset yields. 10y at 7.4-7.5% (3y high). No significant empirical estimate in pack.

evidence.note: India 10y G-sec ~7.4-7.5% in Oct 2026, multi-year high (Reuters/ET headlines); Nov outlook 7.25-7.35%

exposures.mechanism: EBLR/repo-linked loans ~40-45% of domestic book (model knowledge) reprice within a quarter; deposits (global CoD 4.71%) lag. +25bp: ~Rs5 lakh cr x 0.25% = Rs1,250cr gross, ~60% offset by deposit repricing over 6m => NIM +2-3bp ~ Rs500cr/yr = ~2% of annualised PAT Rs26,100cr; x persistence 0.5 x EV/MCap 1.0 => ~+1.0; net of slower credit demand and bond MTM (captured in F_GSEC edge) => +0.5. Sign genuinely uncertain: tightening cycle also lifts credit costs. First hike in ~4 years on 2026-10-07 (calibrated tightening).

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (The Hindu, Reuters headlines)
Q2 FY27 PAT Rs6,532cr +35.8%, NII Rs13,026cr +9%, GNPA 1.78%, NNPA 0.37%

exposures.mechanism: Guidance raised to 13-15% advances growth. +3pp industry growth => BoB avg advances +1.5% (~Rs18,000cr on ~Rs12 lakh cr, model estimate) x net spread ~2.7% (yield 7.41% less marginal funding ~4.7%) = ~Rs490cr, less opex/provisions => ~Rs300cr post-tax = ~1.2% of PAT; x persistence 0.5 x EV/MCap 1.0 plus small re-rating => ~+1.2.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 presentation summary; global NIM 2.74%, CoD 4.71%, yield on advances 7.41%; FY27 credit growth guidance raised to 13-15%, deposits 11-13% (Moneycontrol/ET Bfsi headlines 2026-10-30)

exposures.mechanism: Deposit growth guided 11-13% vs credit 13-15%; gap filled with costlier CDs/FCNR(B). +3pp deposit growth displaces ~1.5% of funding priced ~120bp above CASA/term deposits => ~3bp NIM => ~Rs570cr/yr pre-tax = ~1.6% PAT; x persistence 0.5 => ~+0.8-0.9.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 presentation summary; global NIM 2.74%, CoD 4.71%, yield on advances 7.41%; FY27 credit growth guidance raised to 13-15%, deposits 11-13% (Moneycontrol/ET Bfsi headlines 2026-10-30)

exposures.mechanism: +50bp credit cost x ~Rs12 lakh cr advances = Rs6,000cr pre-tax = Rs4,500cr post-tax = ~17% of annualised PAT Rs26,100cr; EV/MCap 1.0; persistence 0.4 (cycle reverses over 1-2 yrs) => ~-6.9; trimmed to -6.0 because stock already at 0.74x P/B discounts a worse cycle. Current: GNPA 1.78% (2.16% yr ago), NNPA 0.37%, Q2 provisions Rs2,382cr.

exposures.mechanism: Retail unsecured (personal loans+cards) ~6-7% of advances (model estimate) = ~Rs78,000cr; +1pp delinquency x LGD 70% = ~Rs550cr pre-tax = ~1.6% of PAT; x persistence 0.4 => ~-0.6. Much smaller than for private banks/NBFCs.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 PAT Rs6,532cr +35.8%, NII Rs13,026cr +9%, GNPA 1.78%, NNPA 0.37%

exposures.mechanism: RBI expected-credit-loss (ECL) transition: Canara Bank disclosed a one-time hit of Rs12-15k cr on a similar ~Rs12 lakh cr book (2026-10-15, stock -6%). Assume BoB comparable Rs8-12k cr (model assumption, not disclosed) = ~6-9% of Rs1.29 lakh cr mcap pre-tax, absorbed through reserves over 1-2 yrs, CET1 impact limited by strong profit. Market partly priced (BoB held up on Q2). Also HTM MTM scrutiny.

evidence.note: Canara ECL one-time provision up to Rs15,000cr, CET1 12.8%

exposures.mechanism: +Rs1 lakh cr surplus liquidity lowers CD/CP costs and money-market rates, helping CoF by ~2bp on ~Rs19 lakh cr earning assets (NII 13,026x4/2.74%) => ~Rs380cr = ~1.5% PAT x persistence 0.25 => ~+0.4. Oct 2026 liquidity-tightening measures (ET 2026-10-12) are a headwind.

evidence.note: 10y at 3y high as RBI liquidity measure weighs

exposures.mechanism: PSU banks are lead lenders to infra/PSU capex. +10% govt capex growth => corporate credit +~0.7pp for BoB (corporate ~40% of book) => PAT +~0.9% plus lower slippages; x persistence 0.5 => ~+0.8.

FIIs hold 10.3% (up from 9.7% in Mar 2026); +US$5bn/qtr FPI inflow ~ +3% Nifty, BoB beta 1.17 => ~+3.5% broad-market effect, of which ~half is stock-specific reweighting toward PSU banks; the Director's cross-sectional demeaning removes the market part.

Large UAE/GCC franchise and NRI deposit/remittance fees; FCNR(B) deposits are guided to support H2 funding. +10% remittances => CASA/NRI deposits +~1% and fee income +~Rs100cr => ~+0.5% PAT; x persistence 0.5 => ~+0.4.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 presentation summary; global NIM 2.74%, CoD 4.71%, yield on advances 7.41%; FY27 credit growth guidance raised to 13-15%, deposits 11-13% (Moneycontrol/ET Bfsi headlines 2026-10-30)

exposures.mechanism: International book ~Rs2 lakh cr (~15% of advances; UAE/Gulf/Africa; model estimate); escalation (Brent already 95) raises Gulf credit costs and disrupts FCNR inflows; also legacy NMC Health (Abu Dhabi) fraud legal tail. +1 escalation => international PAT (~20% of group, model estimate) -5% => -1% PAT; x persistence 0.5, rounded up for tail risk.

Pack shows significant co-movement (+2.92 per +15% iron ore, t +2.1) but there is no direct link; metals/mining ~5-7% of corporate book and rising steel/ore prices improve cash flows of large borrowers (lower slippages). Fundamental estimate ~+0.4; shrunk toward data only modestly because co-movement is largely cyclical beta (market beta 1.17).

Subsidiaries/associates (BoB Capital, BoB Financial; NSE stake monetisation gains in Q2 FY27 per Rediff headline 2026-10-30) gain from retail financialisation; small share of group value (~3-5%) => +0.5.
